The Windows 10 display settings allow you to change the appearance of your desktop and customize it to your liking. There are many different display settings you can adjust, from adjusting the brightness of your screen to choosing the size of text and icons on your monitor. Here is a step-by-step guide on how to adjust your Windows 10 display settings.

1. Find the Start button located at the bottom left corner of your screen. Click on the Start button and then select Settings.

2. In the Settings window, click on System.

3. On the left side of the window, click on Display. This will open up the display settings options.

4. You can adjust the brightness of your screen by using the slider located at the top of the page. You can also change the scaling of your screen by selecting one of the preset sizes or manually adjusting the slider.

5. To adjust the size of text and icons on your monitor, scroll down to the Scale and layout section. Here you can choose between the recommended size and manually entering a custom size. Once you have chosen the size you would like, click the Apply button to save your changes.

6. You can also adjust the orientation of your display by clicking the dropdown menu located under Orientation. You have the options to choose between landscape, portrait, and rotated.

7. Next, scroll down to the Multiple displays section. Here you can choose to extend your display or duplicate it onto another monitor.

8. Finally, scroll down to the Advanced display settings section. Here you can find more advanced display settings such as resolution and color depth.

By making these adjustments to your Windows 10 display settings, you can customize your desktop to fit your personal preference. Additionally, these settings can help improve the clarity of your monitor for a better viewing experience.

entry.title: Exploring PCDJ's Future Objectives in 2019: An In-Depth Analysis
entry.content:
Exploring PCDJ’s Future Objectives in 2019: An In-Depth Analysis

With 2018 now in the rear-view mirror we look ahead at some of what’s in store for the PCDJ brand and supported services in 2019.

Last week we provided a review of PCDJ’s 2018 and some of the goals we set forth that our company accomplished — now we shift our focus on the future and take a look at some of what’s in store for PCDJ in 2019.

The DJ Software and Karaoke Software market is a highly-competitive space, so we’ll touch lightly on much of what’s up our sleeve for 2019 — but certainly not all.

Disclaimer: This post includes affiliate links

If you click on a link and make a purchase, I may receive a commission at no extra cost to you.

Goals For PCDJ In 2019

  • Release SoundCloud integration for DEX 3, DEX 3 RE, and quite potentially, LYRX | The first item on our list is also the most eminent. As announced at the Amsterdam Dance Event in October, in-app support for SoundCloud’s subscription service is coming to our DJ mixing software . Customers will be able to access 190 million songs from popular artists and SoundCloud producers without ever leaving the software browser, all for only $9.99-a-month. Look for an announcement in the not-to-distant future.
  • Remote Singer/Song Request Platform for DEX 3 and LYRX | We will release a remote singer/song request application that seamlessly integrates with our latest karaoke software platforms, DEX 3 and LYRX. It will sync with your DEX 3 and/or LYRX browser and allow singers to view your karaoke song book (or music list) and make song requests from their own phone or mobile device.
  • More Karaoke | Our core customers have spoken and it’s clear karaoke features and expansion of karaoke capabilities are a top ‘want’. We plan to build on the last few months of karaoke-specific updates to DEX 3 and LYRX that included managed singer rotation, singer/song history, support for karaoke.net (Party Tyme) and more. You’ll see new rotation options and singer management features, among other items.
  • DJ Controller Support | New controllers seem to come out on a weekly basis and we know you want native plug-and-play support in DEX 3 or DEX 3 RE. We’ll continue to map the latest DJ controllers as they become available. Support for the Denon DJ MCX8000 is coming very soon, with a few other maps for new controllers also underway.
  • Karaoke.net Store Coming to Karaoki | Among some other updates and tweaks to existing features, Karaoki will soon be updated with support for Karaoke.net, one of the leading providers of karaoke music. Customers will be able to browse, search, purchase, and download karaoke songs from Karaoke.net without ever leaving the Karaoki browser.
  • Expanded Video Mixing Features and Slideshow | While much has been improved regarding DEX 3 and the karaoke side of things over the last year, and quite a few new video related options have been added, we plan to further focus on improving overall video support, including new transition effects, live camera feed, and the much sought-after ‘slide show’ (display images with transitions while mixing music).

  • New “Engine” | Technology is ever evolving and new methods for coding and development tools continue to improve. The Windows 10 display settings allow you to change the appearance of your desktop and customize it to your liking. There are many different display settings you can adjust, from adjusting the brightness of your screen to choosing the size of text and icons on your monitor. Here is a step-by-step guide on how to adjust your Windows 10 display settings.

1. Find the Start button located at the bottom left corner of your screen. Click on the Start button and then select Settings.

2. In the Settings window, click on System.

3. On the left side of the window, click on Display. This will open up the display settings options.

4. You can adjust the brightness of your screen by using the slider located at the top of the page. You can also change the scaling of your screen by selecting one of the preset sizes or manually adjusting the slider.

5. To adjust the size of text and icons on your monitor, scroll down to the Scale and layout section. Here you can choose between the recommended size and manually entering a custom size. Once you have chosen the size you would like, click the Apply button to save your changes.

6. You can also adjust the orientation of your display by clicking the dropdown menu located under Orientation. You have the options to choose between landscape, portrait, and rotated.

7. Next, scroll down to the Multiple displays section. Here you can choose to extend your display or duplicate it onto another monitor.

8. Finally, scroll down to the Advanced display settings section. Here you can find more advanced display settings such as resolution and color depth.

By making these adjustments to your Windows 10 display settings, you can customize your desktop to fit your personal preference. Additionally, these settings can help improve the clarity of your monitor for a better viewing experience.
